question.:question/problem: Find the exact solution of the equation $8^{x}=40.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We take $\log_{8}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}8^{x}&=40\\\log_{8}(8^{x})&=\log_{8}(40)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b(b^c)=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x=\log_{8}(40).
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\log_{8}(40)$.

First, we take $\log_{8}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}8^{x-3}&=12\\\log_{8}(8^{x-3})&=\log_{8}(12)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b(b^c)=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x-3=\log_{8}(12).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3&=\log_{8}(12)\\x&=\log_{8}(12)+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\log_{8}(12)+3$.
